summary: E-CI-DOM's test-portability finding is valid and requires the authorized R-CI-BROWSER launcher repair plus fresh managed-browser CI verification. No CI outcome is claimed. The dated E-CI-DOM receipt also retains stale undated paths in source_scope despite its byte-identical relocation note; the repair packet should document canonical dated paths and preserve the consumed original bytes.

findings.summary: Both browser tests pass executablePath as CHROMIUM_PATH || /tmp/chromium, bypassing the existing chromiumLaunchOptions helper. The workflow installs Playwright-managed Chromium but does not set CHROMIUM_PATH; a runner without /tmp/chromium will fail before renderer assertions.
findings.classification: valid source/workflow portability gap; not an observed CI failure
findings.required_gate: Use chromiumLaunchOptions(process.env.CHROMIUM_PATH) in both tests and verify with fresh managed-browser CI.

findings.summary: The dated E-CI-DOM receipt source_scope points to absent undated report/receipt paths. The location-correction note verifies byte-identical relocation and the current dated file hashes, so this is stale metadata rather than evidence content drift.
findings.required_gate: Document the canonical dated paths and the historical location correction in the repair packet; do not rewrite consumed E-CI-DOM bytes.

execution.method: read-only source, workflow, report/receipt, relocation-note, and local-log audit

limits: The review confirms a source-level managed-browser portability issue but does not claim CI has failed or passed.
Integrated four-app/five-fixture conformance is outside this review and remains pending fresh CI artifacts.
